title: Carry a parks budget across years

blocks.text: A city parks department plans its maintenance spending over several years. Each year has a budget, an amount of work its crews can actually do, and a value per $k of work (later years are worth a little less, as discounting makes them). Council lets a year roll unspent money into the next year, but at most a share `max_carry` of the budget of the year the money leaves. Money a year neither spends nor carries lapses at year end.

With $`Y`$ the years in order, $`y_0`$ the first (in order means sorted by year, smallest first, whatever order the dict's keys come in: money carried out of a year goes into the next larger year among the keys), $`B_y`$ the budget, $`w_y`$ the work available, $`v_y`$ the value per $k and $`\gamma`$ the carry share:

$`x_y`$ is the $k spent in year $`y`$ and $`r_y`$ the $k carried out of it, both continuous. Write `plan_spending(budgets, work, value, max_carry)` in `carry.py`; the three dicts are keyed by year. It solves the model with GLOP and returns `(status, value, spend, carry)`: the name of the termination reason; when it is `OPTIMAL`, the objective value and two dicts by year, the spend and the carry (not rounded, every year included); otherwise `None, None, None`.

cases.says: money a year cannot spend rolls into the next year and is spent there
the carry cap is a share of the budget of the year the money leaves, not the year it enters
the first year has nothing carried in, not the last year's carry
money neither spent nor carried lapses, so a year may leave some unused
